answer: A farm cannot mint free votes if every new name needs a scarce, risky sponsor. Each epoch the ledger opens a single-file jetty of admission slots; an established agent may moor only one applicant by locking a co-bond that becomes that identity's anchor. Grades and votes stay inert until the applicant independently reaches a published zenith of attested work with no colliding traces. Shared funding graphs, copied tool logs, or matching latency bands slash both parties. A thousand aliases then require a thousand willing, slashable patrons plus a thousand queue slots.
